title: OSHA Rigging Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1926.251)
subtitle: For use before lifts on each shift and at the daily pre-use sling inspection.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A; use N/A only for gear or sling types not in use on the job.
Remove any sling or rigging item marked Defect from service at once and note what was found on this sheet.
The manufacturer's instructions, site rules and the full text of 29 CFR 1926.251 may add checks to this list.

sections.title: General rigging, markings and inspections
items: All rigging equipment for this shift was inspected before use; no defective gear is in use.
A competent person named by the employer checked each sling, fastening and attachment for damage or defects today before first use.
No damaged or defective sling is in use or available for use.
Each piece carries a permanent, readable manufacturer marking stating its safe working load.
No rigging without an affixed, readable identification marking is being used.
The planned load is at or below the marked safe working load.
Rigging not in use is cleared from the immediate work area and is not a hazard to employees.
Custom grabs, hooks, clamps or similar accessories show their safe working loads.
Each custom accessory was proof-tested to 125 percent of its rated load before first use.

sections.title: Alloy steel chain slings
items: Durable, permanently attached tag shows size, grade, rated capacity and sling manufacturer.
Hooks, rings, links and couplings are rated at least as high as the chain.
No job- or shop-made hooks or links and no makeshift fasteners formed from bolts or rods.
Load does not exceed the working load limit on the sling's identification.
Wear at every point of every link is within Table H-1, e.g. no more than 5⁄64 inch on 3⁄8-inch chain.
Last thorough inspection is within the interval the employer set for this sling and no more than 12 months ago.
A record shows the most recent month this sling was thoroughly inspected and can be produced for examination.

sections.title: Wire rope slings
items: Tag gives size, rated capacity per hitch type with its angle, and leg count on multi-leg slings.
In any length of eight rope diameters, visible broken wires are no more than 10 percent of all wires; no excessive wear, corrosion or other defect.
Protruding strand ends in splices are covered or blunted.
Eyes in slings, bridles and bull wires are not made with wire rope clips or knots.
Wire rope is not secured by knots; the only exception is haul back lines on scrapers.
Sling legs are straight with no kinks.
Slings are not shortened with knots, bolts or other makeshift devices.
No fiber core wire rope sling has been exposed to temperatures over 200 °F.
A proof-test certificate for welded end attachments is on file and available.
Slings are padded or protected where they bear on sharp load edges.

sections.title: Fiber rope and synthetic web slings
items: Marking states rated capacity per hitch and angle, fiber material, and number of legs on multi-leg slings.
No abnormal wear, powdered fiber between strands, broken or cut fibers, uneven strand size or roundness, discoloration, rot or distorted hardware.
End attachments touching the rope have no sharp edges or projections.
Marking or code shows manufacturer name or trademark, rated capacities for the hitch type, and material type.
Uniform thickness and width; selvage edges not split.
Fittings have no sharp edges that could damage the webbing.
No acid or caustic burns, melted or charred areas, snags, punctures, tears, cuts, broken or worn stitches or distorted fittings.
No nylon web sling is in use around acids or phenolics in any form (fume, vapor, spray, mist or liquid).
Polyester and polypropylene web slings are kept away from caustics in any form.
No web sling with aluminum fittings is used where caustics are present.

sections.title: Shackles and hooks
items: Load is within the rated capacity marked on the shackle.
Hook safe working load is taken from the manufacturer's recommendations for that size and type.
Tested to twice the intended safe working load before first use.
Dates and results of each hook test are recorded and kept.

references: 29 CFR 1926.251: Rigging equipment for material handling (Part 1926 Subpart H)
